_doc: Analyzer mutants against the double-run oracle (RFC 308a52c3 Д3, phase 2, task 2588fa84): the RFC criterion «a mutant that breaks the skeleton reddens the oracle on at least one corpus query» on the SYNTHETIC corpus — O2 (the oracle's own verdict) is red for every skeleton, fail-safe and walker mutant, not only the entry's verdict axis. M1–M42 take `from`/`to` of query-predicate-analyzer-308a52c3.spec.json (the analyzer's own matrix): a change of the analyzer moves both. M50/M51 are oracle-specific: M51 removes both barriers of the membership entry O1.3 with one anchor (ITRV §A159). O1.20 (the empty answer) carries no mutant by construction: a cut only removes triples and the entry has no negation, so its empty answer stays empty under any skeleton mutant — it is the witness of O2's «one empty judged», whose mutant is K26 in query-prune-oracle-2588fa84.spec.json. Measured 2026-11-13, re-measured 2026-11-14 after review round 2, control 0. `tree`/`subject` are placeholders (§A145).

M1_no_subproperty_widening._note: skeleton (sub-properties): every sub-property entry diverges — the parent and child patterns, the subquery, the count and the LIMIT 1 entry (O1.1, O1.2, O1.9, O1.10, O1.18, O1.19) — and the oracle reddens (O2); no sub-property source is left for the canary (O4); O13 takes the sub-property entry. Axes O30, O30b, O31 (review round 2) drive the sub-property entry: its cut now diverges, so its verdict is no longer equal.

M13_widening_without_declarations._note: skeleton (sub-property declarations): the decorator cannot build its index on the cut — every widened entry diverges (O1.1, O1.2, O1.9, O1.10, O1.18, O1.19, O2); O13 — as M1. Axes O30, O30b, O31 (review round 2) drive the sub-property entry: its cut now diverges, so its verdict is no longer equal.

N5_first_subproperty_only._note: skeleton (closure truncated to the first sub-property): the grandchild edge is lost on the parent entries (O1.1, O1.9, O1.10, O1.18, O2); the child entry has a one-element closure and stays equal, and so does the LIMIT 1 entry (its first row survives). Axes O30, O30b, O31 (review round 2) drive the sub-property entry: its cut now diverges, so its verdict is no longer equal.

M2_bridge_without_rdfs_label._note: skeleton (class bridge without rdfs:label — the only LITERAL label the bridge indexes): the hierarchy entry and the constant-subject path lose their rows (O1.4, O1.11, O2).

M14_hierarchy_triple_no_bridge._note: skeleton (a hierarchy pattern does not pull the bridge): the hierarchy entry diverges (O1.4, O2) and leaves no bridge predicate for the canary (O3).

M3_prune_on_variable_predicate._note: fail-safe (variable predicate): both variable-predicate entries are cut and diverge (O1.12, O1.15, O2).

M4_prune_zero_length_free_subject._note: fail-safe (zero-length path, free subject): the both-ends-free path pairs every node of the graph — the cut has fewer (O1.13, O2).

M5_namespace_filter_scope_unchecked._note: fail-safe (namespace filter in another group): the outer variable predicate is cut to flow# and diverges (O1.15, O2).

M6_byuuid_not_full_load._note: fail-safe (exo:byUUID): the statement-edge subject has no exo:Asset_uid — absent from the cut, found in the full graph (O1.14, O2).

M50_query_predicates_dropped.to: for (const predicate of [] as string[]) add(predicate, "query");
M50_query_predicates_dropped._note: the query's own predicates are not put into P': every entry whose predicate is not also a skeleton predicate diverges (O1.1, O1.2, O1.6–O1.10, O1.16–O1.18, O2); the axes that drive single entries see it too — the plain entry's cut loses more than the one injected row (O6) and is no longer equal (O9), the sub-property entry O13 drives is no longer equal; on the membership entry Instance_class is now in P' ONLY through the class bridge, so the bridge canary drops it and stops being silent (O14, O24). The membership and hierarchy entries themselves stay equal — Instance_class and the hierarchy predicates come in through the bridge too; M51 is their mutant. Axes added after review round 2: the sub-property entry is no longer equal (O30, O30b, O31); the plain entry's cut loses every row, so a reordered cut is diverged, not order-only (O32); the plain and the flow-note entries now share the empty P', so [A, B, A] builds the cut once (O36b).
